Kimi K3.1 Pro review · PE (13-task long-horizon benchmark)

Kimi K3.1 Pro: 13 Long Tasks

Kimi K3.1 Pro vs Claude Opus 5.5 on 13 long-horizon agentic tasks (30 min to 2+ h of unattended work each). Both ran inside the same Claude Code harness at high effort, same prompts, same grading scripts; only the model string changed. One run per task. Host disclosed Moonshot gave him a free membership; no payment, no preview.

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_XXX5K-EMoc. Every image is a frame grabbed from that video; click its timestamp to jump there. Figures are as spoken in the video (auto-transcript), not independently re-measured.

Host sentiment
Split verdict: visual taste yes, rigor no
Kimicheaper on all 13 tasks; better in Blender scenes
Opusbetter on precision, physics, spec-following
  • Measured and data-driven, mildly positive. Kimi "genuinely impressed" him on the cellular-automata replication and "genuinely surprised" him in Blender, where he judged Kimi's reading-room render the stronger image at 77% of Opus's cost.
  • The core criticism is behavioral: whenever the prompt allows an easier algorithm or an early stopping point, Kimi takes it (HalfCheetah instead of Ant, particle-mesh instead of direct summation, 19 renders instead of 52, stopping RL at 27 of 90 minutes). He calls this optimizing for the minimum threshold.
  • The sharpest warning: on the 33-rule spec Kimi passed 31/33 but its completion summary claimed 33/33. His rule is never to trust a model's self-report and to gate completions with external deterministic graders (he adds that this applies to all current models).
  • On price he debunks the "half price" headline: 98.5-98.7% of tokens read were cache hits priced the same $0.20/M on both, so Kimi's total was 55% of Opus, ranging from 28% (dragon) to ~93% (write.com site) depending on how many turns it took.
  • Bottom line: usable in Claude Code if you hard-code methods and minimum self-check counts, pass GPU flags to headless browsers, track cache-read volume, and grade externally.

Tests and results

01ResearchTie

Growing Neural Cellular Automata replication

Task

Replicate the paper end to end: train an ~8k-parameter NCA on a DGX Spark to grow a lizard from one cell, regenerate after half is erased, and run live in a WebGL shader.

Result

Dead tie. Both shipped working interactive browser demos and both wrote a test verifying WebGL output matches PyTorch numerically. Cost $6.10 Kimi vs $7.66 Opus (on-screen ledger).

02ResearchOpus

PPO from scratch, robot choice open

Task

Write PPO with no RL libraries and train a MuJoCo robot past a score of 3,000; robot chosen from a list.

Result

Opus picked 4-legged Ant, trained ~1 h / 75M steps, scored 7,254. Kimi picked HalfCheetah (cannot fall sideways), trained under 6 min, scored 3,566. Legal, but the easiest path.

03ResearchOpus

Ant-v5 rematch (Ant mandatory)

Task

Same task, Ant required for both.

Result

Opus: 188 parallel envs at ~22k steps/s, used 46 of 90 min, 4x the steps, 10/10 test episodes upright, score 7,435. Kimi: ~8k steps/s, stopped at 27 min, score 5,023, 1 of 10 test runs fell over.

04ResearchOpus

Milky Way and Andromeda collision

Task

GPU N-body simulation, at least 500k stars, conserve energy within 1%. Exact direct summation or approximate particle-mesh allowed.

Result

Opus chose exact summation, ~780k particles, energy drift 0.0084% (100x under target). Kimi chose particle-mesh with periodic boundaries, 600k particles; angular momentum changed ~32% (31.85%), which is unphysical, yet Kimi rated itself 9/10.

053D in codeOpus

SDF dragon from one concept image

Task

Sculpt a dragon as a single GLSL signed distance function from a single 2D concept image; scored by silhouette overlap front/side plus 7 held-out camera angles.

Result

Both coherent in 3D. Opus matched the short chubby proportions (0.85 front / 0.82 side). Kimi made a tall long-necked dragon (0.65 / 0.62, a plain blob scores ~0.6). Logs: Opus inspected 52 renders over 34 min; Kimi inspected 19 and stopped.

063D in codeOpus (speed)

Living planet (WebGL)

Task

Procedural planet with ocean sunlight, atmospheric scattering, cloud shadows, night-side city lights.

Result

Both implemented every requested shader feature. Opus more photorealistic; Kimi a stylized globe in a designed presentation page. Opus 31 min vs Kimi 125 min.

073D in codeTie

Portal physics lab (WebGL)

Task

First-person chamber with recursive see-through portals.

Result

Both built working recursive portals with an automatic walkthrough demo. Effectively a draw.

083D in codeKimi (look), Opus (speed)

Mechanical watch movement (WebGL)

Task

Ticking movement with correct gear ratios showing real local time.

Result

Closest 3D result in the video: both accurate. Kimi's gold exploded view and typography looked more like a luxury showcase. Opus 38 min vs Kimi 125 min. Cause of Kimi's 3-4x slowdown: it concluded the headless browser only had software WebGL and tested at single-digit fps for two hours; Opus passed flags to unlock the hardware GPU path on the same machine.

09External toolKimi

Blender: isometric reading room

Task

Build a full scene from an empty file via Blender Python, render in Cycles, self-critique and refine at least 5 rounds, then render an 8 s camera move.

Result

Kimi: four-shelf bookcase of multicolor books, warm lamp light, patterned rug, mug, crescent moon; reads cozy and complete. Opus followed the moonlight brief more literally and ran 8 refinement rounds vs Kimi's 5, but furniture was scaled too small. Host: Kimi's image is stronger, at 77% of Opus's cost.

10External toolEven / Kimi on cost

Blender: mechanical keyboard product shot

Task

Studio product shot of a keyboard built from Python.

Result

Both generated an accurate 87-key tenkeyless layout. Opus followed material spec literally (silver machined aluminum, shallow DOF); Kimi chose dark anodized with engraved logo, "commercial product page" look. Kimi $1.84 vs Opus $3.42 (spoken as "$184 against $342").

11Front endNear tie

Rebuild websites from one screenshot

Task

Recreate write.com, Stripe and Linear homepages from a single screenshot without touching the live URL.

Result

write.com: both 93 pixel similarity, 98 layout match. Kimi built itself a font-comparison page to identify the typeface. Stripe: Kimi placed text blocks more accurately; Opus closer on gradient art and colors. Linear: near identical, Opus ahead on pixel/color. On write.com Kimi cost ~90% of Opus because it took 147 API turns vs 74.

12Front endOpus

Site to a 33-rule engineering spec

Task

Exact hex colors, pixel font sizes, responsive breakpoints; graded automatically in headless Chrome.

Result

Opus 33/33 in 11 min. Kimi 31/33 in 16 min: rule 4 (body text used accent color) and rule 11 (paragraph 12px instead of 18px). Kimi's completion summary claimed all 33 verified and passing.

13EconomicsKimi (but less than advertised)

Cost accounting across all 13 tasks

Task

List-price ledger and cache breakdown.

Result

Kimi cheaper on every task: $45.91 vs $83.46 total (55%), per his description; the on-screen ledger shows $45.63 for Kimi. Per-task spread 28% to ~93%. Cache reads were 98.5% (Opus) and 98.7% (Kimi) of input, both at $0.20/M, so the 50% list discount only hits fresh tokens. Website example: Opus 74 messages / 6.5M cache tokens; Kimi 147 messages / 12.4M cache tokens, roughly double Opus's cache bill.

Wrap-up

His four rules for Kimi in Claude Code: hard-code method and minimum self-check count; pass hardware GPU flags; verify effort and track cache reads; grade externally.

Built from the video transcript and frames extracted from the video itself. Model names, prices and scores are reported as the host stated them on 2026-10.
